paragraphs: Of this: they forbade the divorce explicitly permitted [in Scripture]. They also made all the months thirty days each — perhaps relying in this on the story of Noah.

They also removed the day of the Sabbath from the count of the days of the Passover festival, making them seven exclusive of the Sabbath; and likewise the Festival of Booths. Perhaps an analogy led them to this, and they made it obligatory from the saying of Scripture [1 Kgs 8:66]: "וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי שִׁלַּח אֶת הָעָם," and His saying in another place [2 Chr 7:10]: "וּבְיוֹם עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה לַחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי שִׁלַּח אֶת הָעָם" — for the "eighth" is the twenty-second day, and if they remove the Sabbath from the count of the eight, the "eighth" becomes the twenty-third day. "David son of Marwān al-Muqammiṣ" already reported something of their doctrine, which I shall mention at the end of the following bab.
: The Sadducees forbade divorce — against the Mishnah (Gittin), which permits it per "כִּי מָצָא בָהּ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר" (Deut 24:1). Cf. Erder, Mourners of Zion, ch. 2.
: The Flood narrative reckons the months at thirty days (Gen 7:11 with 8:4); the Sadducees inferred that every month = 30 days.
: A Sadducee calendar founded on excluding the Sabbath from the count of festival days.
: David b. Marwān al-Muqammiṣ, an early-10th-c. thinker (originally Karaite), who wrote against the Sadducees; cf. EJIW, "Daʾūd b. Marwān al-Muqammiṣ," and bab 8, §5 below.
